articles.deck: The money will be spent over the next year, with the first work starting in December.

articles.title: Plans for Free Tax Clinic Set for Eastgate This Winter
articles.deck: Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public.
body: Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public. Organizers ask guests to bring a dish to share or a little cash for supplies. The event will be held at the Foundry Row fire house, rain or shine, with a backup date set for the following Thursday.
Children are welcome, and volunteers will be on hand to help with parking and set-up.

articles.title: The Marsh Landing Pond Committee Plans Community Garden for Spring
articles.deck: The work is expected to take 7 weeks and will be paid for with $850 raised locally.
body: Ida Wallace, who has lived on Hickory Ridge Road for 7 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at Millrace Green on Tuesday at 7 p.m.

Several residents on Hickory Ridge Road said they had been waiting since 1980 for something like this. The effort began in September when a handful of neighbors met at Millrace Green to talk about community garden.
The Hickory Ridge Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.

body: To the editor: Please keep the crosswalk in the budget. Many of us on Orion Terrace use it every week.
I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the November meeting. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.

body: The effort began in February when a handful of neighbors met at the Hickory Ridge rec center to talk about bike repair clinic. Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Wednesday mornings.
Owen Sandoval, who has lived on Meadow Terrace for 37 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.

articles.title: Council Tables Bus Shelter Ordinance
articles.deck: Supporters and opponents on Fox Avenue disagreed about cost and timing.
body: The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.
Councilmember Sadie Nakamura asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $850. Public works estimates the work will take about 6 weeks once it starts in May.

articles.title: Yolanda Sokolov, 65, Church Organist
articles.deck: Friends remember Yolanda Sokolov for the many years of service to Marsh Landing.
body: Born in Marsh Landing in the years after the war, Yolanda Sokolov spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.

Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Stonebridge Trail Crew in his or her name. Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Marsh Landing.
Yolanda Sokolov died in January at home on Walnut Road, at the age of 65.

articles.title: Then & Now: Dover Lane in 1986 and Today
articles.deck: A photo from the Millrace County Historical Society shows the same corner as it looked decades ago.
body: A 1986 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Dover Lane from the corner of Sycamore Avenue.
Someone took the same picture from the same spot this month, holding the camera at about the same height.
Most of the houses are still standing, though the porches and the trees have changed a good deal.

articles.deck: Supporters and opponents on Prospect Terrace disagreed about cost and timing.
body: Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days. The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first.
